"Trump announces partial ceasefire in Ukraine war as Zelenskyy says deal is 'news to me'"
Photo credits in page: Reuters (Volodymyr Pavlov; Vyacheslav Madiyevskyy), EPA (Daryna Naumova)

Trump on Truth Social: "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" No further details. Announced apparently without consulting Zelenskyy.
Zelenskyy to Axios: "If President Trump negotiated it with Putin - please tell us when the ceasefire begins. We are ready and we will accept it."

"There was no sign that the Kremlin was observing Trump's ceasefire." Per Zelenskyy, Russian drones took to the sky "throughout the day" Sunday; also "unfortunately" several airstrikes including on energy infrastructure.
FIGURES (Zelenskyy): Russians hit thermal power station No 5 in Kharkiv - the latest of MORE THAN 200 STRIKES THIS WEEK against electricity generation and transmission facilities in Ukraine. ANOTHER 17 HITS on gas and oil facilities.

Zelenskyy earlier rebuffed Trump's Saturday demand that Kyiv stop bombing Russian oil refineries; said Moscow must first halt its own "brutal" attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. Any deal to end long-range drone strikes would have to be "reciprocal", backed by "real guarantees".
Zelenskyy on the diesel deal: "weak", would generate "billions" in extra revenue for Putin, enabling him to wage war "even more intensely". Trump said Zelenskyy should "damn well stop" hitting Russian refineries; Ukraine needed a "new leader".
Zelenskyy: it was up to Ukrainians to choose "one or another leader"; told ABC News he would organise elections only if Putin agreed to a "total" 60-day ceasefire.
Saturday, Zelenskyy blamed "Russia and Russia alone": "It is possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so."
Most serious US-Ukraine feud since the Oval Office berating last year. Europe's biggest war since 1945.

SECOND-HAND (blocked outlets, do not use as our sourcing):
- ft.com, citing European officials, reported the US is threatening to stop the procurement system that provides Ukraine with weapons, to press Kyiv to halt deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.
- New York Times reported US officials offered the Kremlin economic incentives for a ceasefire incl. releasing billions in frozen Russian sovereign assets and revisiting a plan to sell parts of Lukoil, benefiting Middle Eastern investors some with "business ties" to US negotiators.
